To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the time courses of the phasic release and facilitation are predicted by a model of calcium diffusion and binding, and that these time courses can be used to determine the time course of the action potential-induced influx of calcium ions into the presynaptic terminal.

At the squid giant synapses, presynaptic action potentials release neurotransmitter phasically, and the magnitude of subsequent release is determined by the submembrane calcium concentration during the previous action potential.

the time course of transmitter release and the time course of facilitation can be understood as consequences of the diffusion of calcium ions in the presynaptic terminal, with a square law relationship between submembrane free calcium and transmitter release.

the time course of transmitter release and the facilitation following a train of presynaptic action potentials are consistent with a presynaptic mechanism of calcium diffusion and binding to a fixed pool of calcium sites.
presynaptic calcium diffusion is an important factor in synaptic facilitation and in the time course of transmitter release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium ions are not only a trigger of release, they are also a modulator of release.

calcium ions diffuse in the cytoplasm of the nerve terminal with a diffusion coefficient of approximately 1 micron squared per msec and that the calcium ions that are released during a presynaptic depolarization are sufficient to account for the observed transmitter release.

the time course of transmitter release is determined by the rate of calcium influx, which is determined by the voltage-gated calcium channel, the rate of calcium binding to fixed sites, and the rate of active extrusion of calcium from the cytoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, at the squid giant nerve terminals, the time courses of the presynaptic calcium signal and the transmitter release are not directly related to each other, and that transmitter release is a function of the submembrane calcium concentration, which is not necessarily a simple function of the presynaptically recorded calcium concentration.
a single calcium influx can lead to a long-lasting increase in the probability of release of transmitter, and that the duration of the facilitation depends on the rate of active extrusion of calcium.

the time courses of synaptic facilitation and the decay of intracellular calcium are determined by the time course of the action potential, the calcium binding and extrusion kinetics and the diffusion of free calcium.
